To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The most important CSFs for KM adoption in SMEs are: (1) top management commitment and support, (2) a clear KM strategy, (3) the use of a knowledge management system, and (4) a supportive organisational culture.
The most important factors for KM adoption in SMEs are the availability of resources and the top management support.
the most critical factors for knowledge management implementation are: top management commitment; knowledge-sharing culture; and a knowledge-management strategy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most important CSFs for implementing KM in SMEs are: senior management support and commitment, the creation of a supportive organisational culture, and the establishment of a knowledge-sharing infrastructure.

the most important CSFs for implementing KM in SMEs are: top management support, organisational culture, human resources management, information and communications technology infrastructure and knowledge-sharing mechanisms, and the least important CSFs are: knowledge acquisition, organisational structure, knowledge codification, knowledge strategy, and knowledge measurement and control.
the most important CSF for KM implementation in SMEs is “organisational culture”, which is closely followed by the factors “leadership”, “organisational strategy” and “organisational learning”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CSFs for implementing KM in an SME are: the need for change management; the need for top management support; the need for an effective knowledge-sharing culture; the need for the availability of appropriate technology; the need for a knowledge-management strategy; the need for knowledge-management policies and procedures; the need for training and education; the need for appropriate knowledge-management tools; the need for adequate resources; the need for performance measurement; and the need for knowledge-sharing processes.
the CSFs for implementing KM in SMEs are not much different from those of large companies.
KM implementation in SMEs is not only feasible but can also be successful if the appropriate CSFs are identified and applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, to succeed in KM implementation, the SMEs need to have an effective top-management support, to have the right culture, to have an effective KM infrastructure, to have an appropriate KM process, to have an adequate human-resource policy and to have a good communication strategy.
, for the SME sector, the CSFs of KM are different from those of large organisations.
SMEs need to understand the importance and value of KM and to be committed to implementing it in order to survive and thrive.
